newsitem.title: USA: Clergy leader detained after admonishing Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Clergy leader detained after admonishing Clinton.

text.p: A National Clergy Council official said Wednesday he had been detained by the Secret Service after admonishing President Clinton at a Christmas-eve service about his veto of a late-term abortion ban.

The Reverend Rob Schenck, general secretary to the council, said Secret Service agents blocked him from leaving the Washington National Cathedral for about 15 minutes and rifled his pockets for identification after he had confronted Clinton, who took communion at the late-night service with his wife and daughter.

Schenck said that while he had been waiting to receive communion, he had leaned over the altar rail toward the president's nearby seat and quietly told Clinton: "God will hold you to account, Mr. President."

"He clearly registered with his face and his eyes that he had heard," Schenck said in a telephone interview. He added that he had scant doubt that Clinton knew he was referring to what critics call "partial-birth abortion."
Clinton has been rebuked by Pope John Paul II, Mother Theresa and evangelist Billy Graham among others for vetoing a ban on the procedure.
Schenck said he had been allowed to return to his seat after taking communion, but had been physically pulled aside by an agent as he sought to leave the cathedral.

He said he had been told he could not contact a lawyer as the agent went through his wallet and pulled his driver's license from it. Another of the agents quoted the president as having complained to the Secret Service that Schenck had "said words" to him, Schenck said. "They never really released me," he said. "I walked away."
The Secret Service did not return phone calls seeking comment. A White House spokesman said he had no comment.
The National Clergy Council groups Catholic, Evangelical, Orthodox and Protestant Church leaders and claims to have 5,000 members.
